introduction_markdown:
**Time allowed: three hours.** This paper contains six questions arranged in three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6).

Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Noiseless calculators may be used.

**Useful data:** $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ or $0.082\ \mathrm{atm\,dm^3\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$; one atmosphere (1 atm) = 1 Pa = $1.01\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$ (as printed); relative atomic masses (RAM): C = 12.0, O = 16.0, S = 32.0, H = 1.0, Cl = 35.5.
incertitudes: Q5(a) : la page de garde ne donne pas la masse atomique relative de l'azote (N = 14.0 utilisé) et le sujet ne mentionne pas l'oxygène ; le reste de 36.0 % est attribué à l'oxygène, ce qui redonne exactement M = 89 (C3H7NO2).

Q5(c)(i) : la formule imprimée (CH3)2CH=CH(C2H5)CH2CH3 est invalide (deux carbones à cinq liaisons). Elle est recopiée telle qu'imprimée ; le corrigé retient la structure vraisemblablement visée (CH3)2C=C(C2H5)CH2CH3 (3-éthyl-2-méthylpent-2-ène) et le signale.
Q5 : points imprimés 8 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 20, cohérents avec « TOTAL = 20 marks ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
An organic compound contains 40.4% carbon, 7.9% hydrogen and 15.7% nitrogen. The molecular mass of the compound is 89.

(i) Calculate the empirical formula of the compound.

(ii) Determine the molecular formula of the compound.

(iii) How can you test for the presence of nitrogen in the compound? *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Empirical formula.** The percentages add up to $40.4 + 7.9 + 15.7 = 64.0\ \%$. The remaining $100 - 64.0 = 36.0\ \%$ is taken to be **oxygen** (it is the only way to reach the printed molar mass of 89; RAM: C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0, and N = 14.0, a value not printed on the cover page).

| Element | % by mass | % / RAM = moles in 100 g | Divide by the smallest (1.121) | Whole-number ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | 40.4 | $40.4/12.0 = 3.367$ | 3.00 | 3 |
| H | 7.9 | $7.9/1.0 = 7.90$ | 7.05 | 7 |
| N | 15.7 | $15.7/14.0 = 1.121$ | 1.00 | 1 |
| O | 36.0 | $36.0/16.0 = 2.250$ | 2.01 | 2 |

**Empirical formula: $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO_2}$.**

**(ii) Molecular formula.** Empirical formula mass $= 3(12.0) + 7(1.0) + 14.0 + 2(16.0) = 89$.

$n = \dfrac{\text{molecular mass}}{\text{empirical formula mass}} = \dfrac{89}{89} = 1$

**Molecular formula: $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO_2}$** (for example alanine, 2-aminopropanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH}$).

**(iii) Test for nitrogen: the Lassaigne (sodium fusion) test.** Heat a small sample strongly with a piece of sodium metal in an ignition tube until red hot, then plunge the hot tube into distilled water in a mortar and grind. The nitrogen is converted to sodium cyanide, $\mathrm{NaCN}$. Boil and filter to obtain the sodium fusion extract. Add freshly prepared iron(II) sulphate solution and boil, then add a little iron(III) chloride and acidify with dilute sulphuric acid: a **Prussian blue** precipitate or colour, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$, shows that nitrogen is present.

(For a compound containing the $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group, nitrogen can also be shown by warming with soda lime or concentrated NaOH, which gives ammonia that turns damp red litmus paper blue.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The amino acid, amino ethanoic acid ($\mathrm{NH_2CH_2COOH}$) has both acidic and basic properties. In neutral solution it forms a zwitterion.

(i) What is a zwitterion?

(ii) Give the structure of the amino acid in acidic, basic and neutral medium.

Acidic: ......  Basic: ......  Neutral: ......

(iii) State the type of reaction taking place when two molecules of aminoethanoic acid combine.

Give the structure of the product. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A zwitterion is a **dipolar ion**: a species that carries **both a positive and a negative charge** on different atoms of the same molecule, so that its overall charge is zero. In an amino acid the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group has lost a proton to the $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group, giving $-\mathrm{COO^-}$ and $-\mathrm{NH_3^+}$.

**(ii)**

- **Acidic medium** (excess $\mathrm{H^+}$, the carboxylate group is protonated; the ion is a cation): $\mathrm{{}^+H_3N{-}CH_2{-}COOH}$
- **Basic medium** (excess $\mathrm{OH^-}$, the $-\mathrm{NH_3^+}$ group loses a proton; the ion is an anion): $\mathrm{H_2N{-}CH_2{-}COO^-}$
- **Neutral medium** (zwitterion): $\mathrm{{}^+H_3N{-}CH_2{-}COO^-}$

**(iii)** The type of reaction is a **condensation reaction** (condensation polymerisation: formation of a peptide, or amide, link with the **loss of a molecule of water**) between the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ of one molecule and the $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ of the other. The product is the dipeptide **glycylglycine**:

$\mathrm{H_2N{-}CH_2{-}CO{-}NH{-}CH_2{-}COOH}$

$2\mathrm{H_2NCH_2COOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2NCH_2CONHCH_2COOH} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

(the $-\mathrm{CO{-}NH}-$ group is the peptide link).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the systematic names of the following compounds.

(i) $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH{=}CH}(\mathrm{C_2H_5})\mathrm{CH_2CH_3}$

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH}(\mathrm{CH_3})_2$ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** As printed, the formula $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH{=}CH}(\mathrm{C_2H_5})\mathrm{CH_2CH_3}$ is not a valid structure (two carbon atoms would carry five bonds). The intended compound is almost certainly $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{C{=}C}(\mathrm{C_2H_5})\mathrm{CH_2CH_3}$: the longest chain containing the double bond has five carbons (pent-2-ene), with a methyl group on carbon 2 and an ethyl group on carbon 3:

**3-ethyl-2-methylpent-2-ene.**

**(ii)** $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_3}$: the longest chain containing the double bond has five carbons, numbered from the end nearer the double bond (double bond at carbon 2), with a methyl group on carbon 4:

**4-methylpent-2-ene** (it exists as the *cis* (Z) and *trans* (E) geometric isomers).

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the specific type of organic reaction mechanism taking place in the following conversions.

(i) $\mathrm{C_6H_6} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{AlCl_3/CH_3Cl}\ } \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_3}$

(ii) $\mathrm{CH_4} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{Cl_2/UV\ light}\ } \mathrm{CH_3Cl} + \mathrm{HCl}$

(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3CHO} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{HCN}\ } \mathrm{CH_3CH(CN)OH}$

(iv) $(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{CBr} \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{OH^-/reflux}\ } (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{COH}$ *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Electrophilic substitution** (Friedel-Crafts alkylation): $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (a halogen carrier) polarises $\mathrm{CH_3Cl}$ to produce the electrophile $\mathrm{CH_3^+}$, which substitutes a hydrogen atom of the benzene ring.

**(ii)** **Free-radical substitution**: initiated by UV light which splits $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ homolytically into chlorine radicals ($\mathrm{Cl\cdot}$); propagation steps $\mathrm{Cl\cdot} + \mathrm{CH_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3\cdot} + \mathrm{HCl}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3\cdot} + \mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3Cl} + \mathrm{Cl\cdot}$.

**(iii)** **Nucleophilic addition**: the cyanide ion, $\mathrm{CN^-}$, a nucleophile, attacks the partially positive carbon of the $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ group; the oxygen then picks up a proton from HCN, giving the cyanohydrin (2-hydroxypropanenitrile).

**(iv)** **Nucleophilic substitution**, unimolecular ($S_N1$): the tertiary halogenoalkane first ionises slowly to a tertiary carbocation $(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C^+}$ and $\mathrm{Br^-}$, then the hydroxide ion (nucleophile) attacks the carbocation rapidly.
